subject: Model comparison through hierarchical specification in Stan

messages.author: 60cb13080ab33600
messages.subject: Model comparison through hierarchical specification in Stan
parts:
Hi Stan users, 

Thanks in advance for your help to a relatively new student of Bayesian methods and the use of Stan, and apologies for the long message.

I am a forest ecology PhD student currently taking a course on Bayesian methods at the University of Maine using John Kruschke's 2011 'Doing Bayesian Data Analysis' textbook. Though I like the book overall, one of the downsides (for me personally) has been that a lot of the programming tasks have already been accomplished for the student. Therefore for my own edification in both the theoretical and programming aspects of Bayesian analysis I am attempting to translate some of the JAGS models Kruschke uses into Stan (I am working with rstan and R2jags).

So far this has been relatively straightforward with one exception. One approach that Kruschke emphasizes is model comparison through hierarchical specification with different parameters indexed according to model as a way to estimate the posterior probabilities of the two models and thereby compare them. A good example of this is his hierarchical binomial 'Filtration - Condensation' model. A slightly modified data description and JAGS model that Kruschke specifies are as follows.

data <- list(z = nCorrOfSubj, # number of successes in Bernoulli trials
             n = nTrlOfSubj, # number of trials
             cond = CondOfSubj, # condition of subject
             nSubj = length(CondOfSubj), # total number of subjects
             nCond = length(unique(CondOfSubj))) # total number of conditions

jm1 <- function(){
  
  # Likelihood
  for (i in 1:nSubj){
    z[i] ~ dbin(theta[i], n[i])
    theta[i] ~ dbeta(aBeta[cond[i]], bBeta[cond[i]])
  }
  
  # Prior
  for (j in 1:nCond){
      aBeta[j] <- mu[j]     * (kappa[j]*equals(mdlIdx,1)+kappa0*equals(mdlIdx,2))
      bBeta[j] <- (1-mu[j]) * (kappa[j]*equals(mdlIdx,1)+kappa0*equals(mdlIdx,2))
  }

  # Hyperprior on mu and kappa:
  kappa0 ~ dgamma( shk0[mdlIdx] , rak0[mdlIdx] )
  for ( j in 1:nCond ) {
    mu[j] ~ dbeta( aHyperbeta , bHyperbeta )
    kappa[j] ~ dgamma( shk[j,mdlIdx] , rak[j,mdlIdx] )
  }
  
  # Constants for hyperprior:
  aHyperbeta <- 1
  bHyperbeta <- 1
  
  # Actual priors:
  shP <- 1.0 # shape for prior
  raP <- 0.1 # rate for prior
  # shape, rate kappa0[ model ]
  shk0[2] <- shP
  rak0[2] <- raP
  # shape kappa[ condition , model ]
  shk[1,1] <- shP
  shk[2,1] <- shP
  shk[3,1] <- shP
  shk[4,1] <- shP
  # rate kappa[ condition , model ]
  rak[1,1] <- raP
  rak[2,1] <- raP
  rak[3,1] <- raP
  rak[4,1] <- raP
  
  # Pseudo priors:
  # shape, rate kappa0[ model ]
  shk0[1] <- 54.0
  rak0[1] <- 4.35
  # shape kappa[ condition , model ]
  shk[1,2] <- 11.8
  shk[2,2] <- 11.9
  shk[3,2] <- 13.6
  shk[4,2] <- 12.6
  # rate kappa[ condition , model ]
  rak[1,2] <- 1.34
  rak[2,2] <- 1.11
  rak[3,2] <- 0.903
  rak[4,2] <- 0.748
  
  # Hyperprior on model index:
  mdlIdx ~ dcat( modelProb[] )
  modelProb[1] <- 0.003
  modelProb[2] <- 0.997
}

I am attempting to specify a simpler model that still retains the model comparison features. For those with access to the Kruschke text, this model is for the thematic apperception test data on page 317-318.

My data, stan code, and initialization follows:


tat.data <- list(nMod = 2,
                 nCond = 2,
                 nSubj = 40,
                 Cond = c(rep(1, 20), rep(2, 20)),
                 N = rep(10, 40),
                 z = c(8, 4, 6, 3, 1, 4, 4, 6, 4, 2, 2, 1, 1, 4, 3, 3, 2, 6, 3, 4,
                       2, 1, 1, 3, 2, 7, 2, 1, 3, 1, 0, 2, 4, 2, 3, 3, 0, 1, 2, 2))


tat.comp <-'
  data{
    int <lower = 0> nSubj;
    int <lower = 0> nCond;
    int <lower = 0> Cond[nSubj];
    int <lower = 0> N[nSubj];
    int <lower = 0> z[nSubj];
    int <lower = 1, upper = 2> nMod;
  }

  parameters{
    real <lower = 0, upper = 1> theta[nSubj];
    real <lower = 0, upper = 1> mu[nCond];
    real <lower = 0, upper = 1000> kappa[nCond];
    real <lower = 0, upper = 1000> kappa0;
    vector[nMod] modProbs;
  }
  
  transformed parameters {
    real <lower = 0, upper = 100> a[nCond];
    real <lower = 0, upper = 100> b[nCond];
    real <lower = 0, upper = 100> muA;
    real <lower = 0, upper = 100> muB;
    real <lower = 0, upper = 100> shK;
    real <lower = 0, upper = 100> rK;
    muA <- 3.5;
    muB <- 6.5;
    shK <- 10;
    rK <- 0.1;
    if(nMod == 1)
      for (i in 1 : nCond){
        a[i] <- mu[i] * kappa[i];
        b[i] <- (1 - mu[i]) * kappa[i];
      }
    else
      for(i in 1 : nCond){
        a[i] <- mu[i] * kappa0;
        b[i] <- (1 - mu[i]) * kappa0;
      }
  }

  model{
    modProbs ~ beta(2, 2);
    nMod ~ categorical(modProbs);
    for (i in 1 : nSubj){
      z[i] ~ binomial(N[i], theta[i]);
      theta[i] ~ beta(a[Cond[i]], b[Cond[i]]);
    }
    for (i in 1 : nCond){
      mu[i] ~ beta(muA, muB); 
      kappa[i] ~ gamma(shK, rK);
    }
    kappa0 ~ gamma(shK, rK);
  }
'
inits <- function(){
  list(theta = c(runif(40, 0, 1)), 
       mu = c(runif(2, 0, 1)),
       kappa = c(runif(2, 0, 100)),
       kappa0 = runif(1, 0, 100),
       nMod = rbinom(n = 1, size = 1, prob = 0.5) + 1,
       modProbs = c(runif(2, 0, 1)))
}

I can initialize and run stan with this model, but it fails to converge in such a way that leads me to believe there is a problem with the model specification. Kruschke makes a point of defining pseudopriors (which is still beyond me, I confess - is this part of the problem?), but I was hoping to get help here in diagnosing the (unquestionable) programming errors on my end.

Thanks again,

Nathan Rutenbeck
University of Maine School of Forest Resources

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model comparison through hierarchical specification in Stan
parts:
That's a large model to try to diagnose.

My suggestion would be to do a line-for-line translation
and work from there. For instance, I don't see the equivalent
of this piece of JAGS code in your Stan model:

Alternatively, try a much simpler model and build up from
there.

We didn't really build Stan with model comparison in mind.
There are a couple of issues:

1. Stan's reported lp__ values are the log probability on the
unconstrained parameters, which is the model log probability
plus the log Jacobians of the transforms (described in a
later chapter in the Stan manual). Your message reminded me we
want to break that down, so I created a feature request:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/448

2. Stan's reported lp__ values drop any additive constants
on the log scale (multiplicative constants on the linear scale)
that arise from sampling statements. You can get the full
log probabilities at the cost of some efficiency by replacing:

y ~ foo(theta);

with

increment_log_prob(foo_log(y,theta));

The latter includes the normalizing constants.

- Bob
